explanation: The theorem says: if x ≠ 0 lies in P (its image in the quotient by P is 0) and P lies over p, then p ≤ |N(x)|. I found no single Mathlib declaration that states this, or anything that gives it in one or two lines. I searched for lemmas about norms dividing or lying in ideals (`dvd_norm`, `norm_mem`, `dvd_absNorm`, and norm-membership lemmas mentioning `under`/`comap`) and read the closest matches. The nearest are `Ideal.absNorm_dvd_norm_of_mem` (the ideal norm of I divides the norm of any x ∈ I), `Ideal.norm_mem_relNorm` / `Ideal.norm_mem_spanNorm`, and `Int.absNorm_under_dvd_absNorm`. Getting the theorem from these would take several steps: turn the quotient hypothesis into membership in P, show p divides the integer norm (either because the norm lies in P ∩ ℤ = (p), or by chaining the divisibility lemmas), then apply Nat.le_of_dvd using positivity of the norm. That is more than the two-line limit. The library's proof also relies on its own helper lemmas (`prime_dvd_integerNorm_of_quotient_eq_zero`, `integerNorm_natAbs_pos`).
